item.title: Black Voters Demand Results and Protection as 2026 Elections Approach
item.description: A new national study examining political opposition and civic engagement within Black communities has found that Black voters are signaling dissatisfaction, caution and conditional readiness to act as the 2026 elections approach, with economic strain and fear of retaliation being major barriers to participation. The post Black Voters Demand Results and Protection as 2026 Elections Approach appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: DC Water Updates Community in Forum Regarding Potomac Interceptor Collapse
item.description: DC Water and Maryland held community forums to address residents' concerns about the Jan. 19 Potomac Interceptor collapse and wastewater overflow, and to provide updates on the rehabilitation and restoration plans for the affected area. The post DC Water Updates Community in Forum Regarding Potomac Interceptor Collapse appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Live Boldly – March 2026 Message From Department of Aging and Community Living
item.description: The Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL) has been working hard to provide vital services to seniors in the District, including providing nearly 900,000 meals in Fiscal Year 2025, expanding nutrition services, and protecting vulnerable adults from abuse and neglect. The post Live Boldly – March 2026 Message From Department of Aging and Community Living appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Women’s History Month: Estate Planning as an Act of Self-Care
item.description: Estate planning is an essential form of self-care for women, particularly Black women, as it provides protection, dignity, and peace of mind, while also preserving generational wealth and ensuring that loved ones are not left guessing or fighting in court. The post Women’s History Month: Estate Planning as an Act of Self-Care appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: U.S. Casualties Mount as D.C. Tightens Security Following Iran Strikes
item.description: President Trump launched a war with Iran without congressional approval, resulting in the deaths of three U.S. service members and scores of civilians, prompting criticism from politicians and organizations for undermining democratic checks and balances. The post U.S. Casualties Mount as D.C. Tightens Security Following Iran Strikes appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Maryland Political Updates: Hakeem Jeffries Talks Redistricting; Moore’s Housing Agenda Moves Forward
item.description: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries discussed redistricting with Senate President Bill Ferguson, but the proposed plan is opposed by multiple Senate Democrats and does not have the support to pass in the Senate. The post Maryland Political Updates: Hakeem Jeffries Talks Redistricting; Moore’s Housing Agenda Moves Forward appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Amid Fletcher-Johnson Redevelopment, Community Members Remember the Good Times
item.description: Dr. George H. Rutherford, former principal of Fletcher-Johnson Middle School, maintained contact with his former students and was honored at a party organized by alumni, who remember him as a courageous leader who provided them with support and structure. The post Amid Fletcher-Johnson Redevelopment, Community Members Remember the Good Times appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Opera Meets the Community: WNO Previews ‘Treemonisha’ and ‘The Crucible’
item.description: The Washington National Opera, in partnership with The Washington Informer, hosted a Spring Preview Performance and Q&A featuring excerpts from "Treemonisha" and "The Crucible" at Busboys & Poets Takoma, with Grammy Award-winning mezzo-soprano J'Nai Bridges and soprano Viviana Goodwin starring in the productions. The post Opera Meets the Community: WNO Previews ‘Treemonisha’ and ‘The Crucible’ appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: With Beleaguered Ward 8 Hospital in the Backdrop, Community Members Organize for Solutions, Alternatives
item.description: Pan-African Community Action (PACA) is coordinating a grassroots medical program to provide free preventative health education, supplies, and screenings to Ward 8 residents in response to long wait times, a nursing shortage, and lack of outpatient services at Cedar Hill Regional Medical Center GW Health. The post With Beleaguered Ward 8 Hospital in the Backdrop, Community Members Organize for Solutions, Alternatives appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Collins D.C. Council Report: Federal Officer Transparency, the Decoupling Impasse, and a Foreign Policy Matter
item.description: The D.C. Council unanimously approved two bills to increase transparency in federal agent use of force, while also discussing the U.S.-Israeli military campaign and other foreign policy matters. The post Collins D.C. Council Report: Federal Officer Transparency, the Decoupling Impasse, and a Foreign Policy Matter appeared first on The Washington Informer.
